content: Eisenhower College was a small educational institution named after President Dwight D. Eisenhower of the United States. It was located in Seneca Falls, New York, and was established as a liberal arts college. The first class of students began their studies in 1968. These courses were mandatory for all students and provided a comprehensive examination of the history of civilization, spanning from the early development of humanity to modern times. The subjects covered in these courses included music, art, history, science, philosophy, and literature. In addition to the core curriculum, students were also required to take courses in foreign languages and physical education. A distinctive feature of the college was its weekly classes in modern music and human sexuality, which were held in a building known as the Red Barn. These classes were well-attended and became a notable aspect of campus life. Another unique tradition at Eisenhower College was the annual Communication Arts Festival, which took place every April. Since the college did not have a fall homecoming tradition, this festival, often referred to as Comm-Arts weekend, served as an opportunity for students, alumni, and friends to reconnect and celebrate together. The event was marked by the rainy spring weather typical of the Seneca Falls area. Eisenhower College graduated its final class in 1983. This followed its acquisition by the Rochester Institute of Technology in 1979. Subsequently, the property was sold to the New York Chiropractic College, which continues to operate on the campus. As of 2006, an archive of materials related to Eisenhower College, donated by former professors and alumni, is preserved on the campus.
